| Initial project label derived from repo folder | **FAIL (frontend)** | Backend derives it (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:127-146`) but the UI never reads it; `ui/src/App.tsx:52` still hardcodes `{ workspaceId: DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID, repoRoot: "." }`. |

### Findings, severity-ranked

**S1 — BLOCKER: "Add Worktree at each project row" is absent.**
`ui/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:196-247` renders the project row (chevron toggle + select button + badges) with **no** add-worktree affordance. The only project-scoped creation path is `WorktreeList`'s `onCreate` (`Sidebar.tsx:263` → `WorktreeList.tsx:44-51`), which renders *only in the empty state* ("Create the first worktree"). A project that already has worktrees has **no** way to add another scoped to it.

Runtime evidence (I rendered `Sidebar` with 2 projects + 1 worktree and enumerated the a11y tree):
```
ADD_WORKTREE_BUTTON_COUNT 1
ARGS [[]]                        # called with zero args → project === undefined
ALL_BUTTONS  Hide sidebar | Add worktree | Add project | Collapse default | default |

             rorca-qa | Settings
```
Exactly one `Add worktree` button, in the titlebar, passing `undefined`. The per-row control does not exist in the DOM. (Probe file removed; tree is clean.)

**S1 — BLOCKER: initial project label is still `"default"` in the UI.**
`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:127-146` slugifies `current_dir().file_name()` and registers it, then at `lib.rs:152-154` *also* registers the alias `"default"` for the same root. Meanwhile `ui/src/App.tsx:52` defines `DEFAULT_PROJECT = { workspaceId: DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID, repoRoot: "." }`, `App.tsx:761-773` (`loadProjects`) falls back to it on first run, and `App.tsx:784-790` (`loadActiveProjectId`) defaults to `"default"`. There is **no IPC to enumerate backend-registered workspaces** — `ui/src/lib/tauri.ts` exposes only `cmd_project_register` / `cmd_project_branches`, and `lib.rs:171-215`'s `invoke_handler` has no list command. On a fresh install the sidebar therefore still reads **"default"**, and `App.tsx:142-146` re-registers `("default", ".")` on mount, so the derived id is never surfaced. The `derived_id != "default"` alias registration exists solely to keep the hardcoded frontend working — it is the tell that the feature was implemented on only one side of the boundary.

**S2 — MAJOR: dead backend command; `detectAgents` will throw at runtime.**
`ui/src/lib/tauri.ts:292` invokes `cmd_agents_detect`. `src-tauri/src/ipc/agents.rs` defines it, but `src-tauri/src/ipc/mod.rs:1-9` never declares `pub mod agents;` and `lib.rs:171-215` never registers it. `rg -n "agents" src-tauri/src --glob '*.rs'` matches **only inside `agents.rs` itself** — the module is entirely unreachable, and its `#[cfg(test)]` tests never compile. `App.tsx:65-77` calls it on mount inside a `try/catch` that only `console.warn`s, so it fails silently in the real app while `App.test.tsx` mocks it green.

**S2 — MAJOR: `createTargetProject` has zero test coverage and is unreachable in production.**
`App.tsx:261` + `App.tsx:610-613` add per-project targeting (`setCreateTargetProject(project ?? activeProject)`) consumed at `App.tsx:693`. The App test mock even renders a `Add worktree to {project.workspaceId}` button (`App.test.tsx:165-167`) — but **no test ever clicks it** (`rg "Add worktree to" ui/src` → one hit, the mock definition only). Combined with S1, the only production caller passes `undefined`, so the branch always resolves to `activeProject`. Dead code plus a test hook that was built and then not used.

**S2 — MAJOR: `AddWorktreeDialog` project switch does not switch the active workspace.**
Even if S1 were fixed, `App.tsx:693` passes `createTargetProject` to the dialog, which calls `listProjectBranches(project.workspaceId)` and `createWorktree({ workspaceId: project.workspaceId, ... })` (`ProjectDialogs.tsx:269, 295-297`) — correct. But `onCreated` (`App.tsx:697-700`) calls `refreshWorktrees()` / `ensureTabForWorktree()`, which are bound to `useWorkspaceStore({ workspaceId: activeProject.workspaceId })` (`App.tsx:127`) and `useWorkspaceRuntime({ workspaceId: activeProject.workspaceId })` (`App.tsx:129`). Creating a worktree in a *non-active* project would spawn its terminal against the **active** project's registry entry. Untested, latent as long as S1 stands.

**S3 — MODERATE: tests assert the old arrangement, so they cannot detect S1.**
- `Sidebar.test.tsx:81-100` ("keeps only global actions in the sidebar titlebar") *codifies* the global Add worktree button as correct — it asserts it lives inside `sidebar-drag-region`. This locks in the wrong layout.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx:220-247` is named "hooks worktree creation… into the owning project group" but its creation assertion is `fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Add worktree" }))` + `expect(onCreateWorktree).toHaveBeenCalledOnce()` — it clicks the **titlebar** button (proven the only match by my probe), never scopes with `within(qaGroup)`, and **never asserts the project argument**. The name claims project scoping; the assertion proves only that a global button fires. This is the single most misleading artifact in the change.
- `Sidebar.test.tsx:249-263` clicks `/create the first worktree/i` but likewise asserts only `toHaveBeenCalledOnce()`, not `toHaveBeenCalledWith(accordionProjects[1])` — the one place per-project wiring *is* live goes unverified.

**S3 — MODERATE: `aria-label`s expose raw slugs, not human labels.**
`Sidebar.tsx:206` (`aria-label={`${expanded ? "Collapse" : "Expand"} ${project.workspaceId}`}`), `:216` (`aria-label={project.workspaceId}`), `:222` (visible text), and `:268` (`label={`${project.workspaceId} worktrees`}`) all render the workspace **id**. Since the naming work is about a user-facing *label*, `RegisteredProject` (`ui/src/lib/tauri.ts`) carrying only `workspaceId`/`repoRoot` means there is no place to put a display name distinct from the identity used for branch namespacing (`orca/<wsId>/<slug>`). Deriving the label by changing the id, as `lib.rs` does, conflates the two.

**S4 — MINOR: backward-compatibility hazard in the dual registration.**
`lib.rs:152-154` swallows the alias result with `let _ =`. `WorkspaceRegistry::register` (`registry.rs:36-52`) returns `Ok(())` for a same-root duplicate and `WorkspaceAlreadyRegistered` otherwise, so the same repo now occupies **two** registry keys. Existing branches are namespaced `orca/default/<slug>`, but new worktrees created under the derived id get `orca/<derived>/<slug>`. `Sidebar.tsx:groupWorktreesByProject` (`:293-311`) buckets by `worktreeIdentity(worktree)?.wsId`, so once the frontend *is* migrated to the derived id, pre-existing `orca/default/*` worktrees fall through to the `activeProjectId` fallback and silently appear under the wrong project. No migration path exists.

**S4 — MINOR: dead code left after the titlebar rewrite.**
`worktreeRegionRef` (`Sidebar.tsx:71`) is still declared and attached at `:177`, but its only consumer — `focusWorktrees` — was deleted (diff removes `Sidebar.tsx` lines 145-149). The ref and `tabIndex={-1}` now serve nothing. `onOpenCommandPalette` was demoted to optional (`Sidebar.tsx:47`) and destructured out of the body but remains in the prop type, and `Sidebar.activity.test.tsx:72,102` still passes it. ### Public prop/API consistency
`onCreateWorktree: (project?: RegisteredProject) => void` (`Sidebar.tsx:44`) is a **backward-compatible widening** — old zero-arg callers still typecheck. `onOpenCommandPalette` went required → optional (`:47`), also non-breaking. `useWorkspaceStore.openTab` gained two optional trailing params (`workspaceStore.ts:201-208`), non-breaking. `npx tsc --noEmit -p ui/tsconfig.json` is clean; `cargo check` compiles with 4 pre-existing unrelated warnings (`worktree/manager.rs` writer-lease dead code) — none introduced here.

Accordion state (`Sidebar.tsx:79-101`) is correctly modeled as the *collapsed* set with per-project independence and a `knownProjectsRef` seed for late-registered projects — this part is well done and genuinely covered (`Sidebar.test.tsx:135-208`). Cross-project worktree selection (`App.tsx:307-320` + the `pendingWorktreePath` handoff at `:322-328`) is correct and covered. The defect is confined to *creation* targeting, not selection.

### Test-coverage assessment
Suites run green — `npx vitest run src/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/App.test.tsx` → **34 passed**. That result is **not** evidence for the requirement: the two assertions that would catch S1 click the global titlebar button and check only call *count*, and no test asserts the derived startup label at all. Coverage of the accordion, persistence, routing, and resize is solid; coverage of the two required behaviors is zero-to-negative (S3 actively pins the wrong layout).

### To reach PASS
